name: Congenital Myasthenic Syndrome Due to Defective Synaptic Vesicles Exocytosis
aliases: CMS with impaired synaptic vesicle release
Synaptic vesicle exocytosis-related congenital myasthenic syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Myasthenic Syndromes

criteria.description: Presence of fatigable muscle weakness with onset in infancy or early childhood
Electrophysiological evidence of impaired neuromuscular transmission such as decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes affecting synaptic vesicle exocytosis (e.g., SYT2, SNAP25)
Improvement of symptoms with acetylcholinesterase inhibitors or 3,4-diaminopyridine

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of fatigable muscle weakness with electrophysiological evidence plus pathogenic genetic variant in synaptic vesicle exocytosis genes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of autoimmune myasthenia gravis and other neuromuscular junction disorders.

searchTerms: muscle weakness that worsens with use

laboratory: Negative acetylcholine receptor and MuSK antibodies
imaging: Chest imaging may show atelectasis or aspiration pneumonia secondary to bulbar weakness
genetic: Pathogenic variants in SYT2, SNAP25, or other genes involved in synaptic vesicle exocytosis
other: Electrophysiological studies showing decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation

distinguishingFeatures: Genetic mutations affecting postsynaptic or presynaptic proteins other than synaptic vesicle exocytosis

redFlags: Poor response or worsening with acetylcholinesterase inhibitors
